correctness.rationale: Every extensive isotone idempotent map on the finite atom diamond is uniquely of type \(A_S\), \(B_i\), or \(C\), as determined by its bottom image and fixed atoms. Composition gives \(A_S\circ A_T=A_{S\cap T}\), distinct \(B_i\) multiply to \(C\), and \(A_S\) commutes with \(B_i\) exactly when \(i\in S\); \(C\) is absorbing. Thus the maximal compatible families are \(\mathcal F_J\) for subsets \(J\subseteq[n]\). Inclusion-exclusion gives the ordered \(k\)-tuple counts, including \(k=0\). Direct exhaustive enumeration verifies the original axioms, commutation graph and maximality through eight atoms, plus selected tuples of lengths up to four. Finite computation corroborates but does not establish the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: Glück’s 2023 Lemma 7.4 counts the \(2^n+n+1\) closure operators on the diamond and describes their closure systems, so that baseline is explicitly excluded from novelty. The final claim adds a full pairwise-commutation geometry, all maximal families, and an arbitrary-arity exponential generating function. Successful semantic published-record queries for diamond closure commutation and arbitrary commuting tuples returned related results about other modal condensations and ordered tuple orbits, not a claim implying the diamond statements. Comparisons with accessible previous findings identify them as distinct relational/modal-algebra or Horn-closure classification problems. A general 1979 common-fixed-point theorem provides no diamond-specific enumerators. Search failure and incomplete full-text access leave a nonzero equivalent-formulation risk.

value.rationale: Pairwise commutation of closure modalities is the intrinsic algebraic condition for order-independent combination. On the first natural nondistributive atom diamonds the theorem gives a complete structural classification of *all maximal* compatible systems, shows exactly which subsets of the \(n\) atomic modal updates may coexist with which fixed-point closures, and solves the arbitrary-multiplicity tuple enumeration. These are natural infinite-parameter invariants, not an arbitrary short enumeration, and the result distinguishes global compatibility from the previously known total count. It makes no claim about downstream complexity gains or transfer to other lattice classes.
